before: Integer.parseInt expects decimal integer text in the accepted range. NumberFormatException identifies a failed parse. In a stack trace, inspect the exception type and first relevant application frame; line numbers change when source changes.
The catch reports a stable message for an expected bad input. It does not claim that every exception has been repaired. Avoid dumping secrets or arbitrary configuration contents into production logs.
Expected output or behavior: expected a whole number. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Remove the catch locally and identify the application frame in the stack trace; do not memorize a line number. You may trace it without a JDK; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: Integer.parseInt reads decimal text that fits in an int. Otherwise it throws NumberFormatException. An unhandled error can show a stack trace: a list of calls that led to it. Start with the error type and the first listed call from your own code; line numbers can change after edits.

This catch handles the expected bad-number error with a short message. It does not handle every possible failure. When recording errors in a real app, report useful details without exposing passwords or other private data.
The program prints expected a whole number. The word many cannot be read as an int, so the normal print receives no number.
The quiz supplies digits that fit in an int. A successful conversion returns normally and skips catch.

before.question: What prints if the input is "12" instead?
choices: The catch runs after every successful parse.
before.explanation: The valid parse returns 12 and execution never enters the catch.

after.question: Use the input "12" instead. What prints?
choices: Both messages, because catch always runs
after.explanation: The text parses successfully as twelve. The print runs normally, so the catch block is skipped.
